web.title: Web
web.lead: From one line in the address bar to pixels on screen — everything in between

git.title: Git
git.lead: Not memorizing commands — seeing the graph. Once you see it, it stops being scary

cs.title: Computer science
cs.lead: The layer that does not follow trends — still true in ten years

shell.title: Linux & shell
shell.lead: While the black window scares you, the server belongs to someone else

devops.title: DevOps & cloud
devops.lead: The layer that lets other people use what you built — where it becomes a service

security.title: Security
security.lead: You see where to defend only after you see how things break

ai.title: AI & LLM
ai.lead: Engineering on the using side — system design, not clever wording

data.title: Data
data.lead: Easy to pile up, hard to get back out — design backwards from the reading side

game.title: Game development
game.lead: Fun is a feeling, not a feature — the distance between running and enjoyable

craft.title: Developer craft
craft.lead: What separates people regardless of language — the part nobody teaches

mobile.title: Mobile
mobile.lead: The screen in your hand plays by other rules — narrow, flaky, battery-powered

scale.title: Distribution & scale
scale.lead: When one machine stops being enough — and the new problems that splitting creates

gfx.title: Graphics & shaders
gfx.lead: Why a pixel is that color — the rules of triangles and light

embed.title: Embedded & IoT
embed.lead: Computers off-screen — kilobytes of memory, and someone has to walk over to unplug it

stages.craft-b: The power to leave something behind

web-html.title: HTML — structure that means something
web-html.why: Build it all out of divs and search engines, screen readers and keyboards all go blind. Tags are meaning, not decoration.
web-html.check: You pick heading, list, table and form tags by name alone

web-css.title: CSS — boxes and flow
web-css.why: Layouts break mostly because nobody drew the box model and the flow first.
web-css.check: You choose flex or grid and can say why

web-js.title: JavaScript fundamentals
web-js.why: Values, scope and async — hold those three and frameworks shrink to syntax.
web-js.check: You can draw closures and the event loop

web-dom.title: DOM and events
web-dom.why: This is exactly what a framework does for you. Only someone who did it by hand can question the framework.
web-dom.check: You build a todo list with no library (add, delete, filter)

web-http.title: HTTP, cache, cookies
web-http.why: Slow, stale, logged out — all three end here.
web-http.check: You explain the difference between 304 and 200 (from cache) in the network tab

web-render.title: The rendering pipeline
web-render.why: Scrolling stutters not because there is a lot of code but because layout is recomputed.
web-render.check: You tell apart properties that cause reflow from those that do not

web-a11y.title: Accessibility and forms
web-a11y.why: A screen you cannot use with a keyboard is a screen that is half built.
web-a11y.check: You unplug the mouse and still get through your own screen

web-devtools.title: Digging in with DevTools
web-devtools.why: Looking instead of guessing. Without this every later step is guesswork.
web-devtools.check: You catch when a value changes using a breakpoint

web-ts.title: TypeScript
web-ts.why: Types are documentation — the only kind you actually leave for yourself six months out.
web-ts.check: You handle someone else's API response without any

web-framework.title: One framework (React / Svelte / Vue)
web-framework.why: Which one matters less than getting the one-way flow from state to screen into your hands.
web-framework.check: You decide where state lives (local, global, server) and say why

web-build.title: Bundlers and modules
web-build.why: If you do not know what the build does, you can do nothing when it breaks.
web-build.check: You find the heavy dependency in a bundle report

web-test.title: Testing (unit and browser)
web-test.why: How you prove a fix. Memory does not stop regressions.
web-test.check: You write the failing test that reproduces the bug first

web-deploy.title: Deploy and observe
web-deploy.why: Working on your machine is still nothing.
web-deploy.check: One push changes the real URL, and something alerts you when it breaks

git-model.title: Commits are snapshots, branches are sticky notes
git-model.why: Believe it stores diffs and rebase and cherry-pick stay magic forever.
git-model.check: You can draw commit, tree, blob and parent

git-areas.title: Working tree, index, HEAD
git-areas.why: This is why add exists as its own step — and where partial commits live.
git-areas.check: From status output alone you say which area each file is in

git-branch.title: Branching and merging
git-branch.why: Branches are cheap. Fear them and everything piles onto one line you cannot unwind.
git-branch.check: You resolve a conflict by hand and explain the result

git-rebase.title: Rebase — rewriting commits
git-rebase.why: The tool that makes history readable — and an accident when used on commits others already pulled.
git-rebase.check: You squash three commits, reorder them, and edit just the middle one

git-undo.title: Undo — reset, revert, reflog
git-undo.why: Git almost never truly loses anything. Learn reflog and your hands get free.
git-undo.check: You recover a commit destroyed by a hard reset

git-remote.title: Remotes — fetch, pull, push
git-remote.why: Once you know pull is fetch plus merge, the weird merge commits stop.
git-remote.check: You explain how origin/main differs from main

git-pr.title: Pull requests, review, commit messages
git-pr.why: Code is written once and read many times. Review is the packaging for the reader.
git-pr.check: The first line of your message says why, not what
links: How to write a Git commit message

git-flow.title: Collaboration strategy (trunk, release, tags)
git-flow.why: With no rule you get one rule per person.
git-flow.check: You can write a paragraph on why your team picked this one

git-bisect.title: Bisect — finding the guilty commit
git-bisect.why: Find when it broke by binary search instead of guessing.
git-bisect.check: You attach a reproduction script and let it run automatically

git-worktree.title: Worktree and stash
git-worktree.why: How to open another branch without breaking what you were doing. Essential once work overlaps.
git-worktree.check: You keep two branches open at the same time

git-hooks.title: Hooks and automated checks
git-hooks.why: A rule survives only when a machine keeps it, not a person.
git-hooks.check: Tests run automatically before a push

cs-binary.title: Number bases, bits, floating point
cs-binary.why: Not knowing why 0.1 + 0.2 looks like that is how money math goes wrong.
cs-binary.check: You give an example of integer overflow and of float error

cs-memory.title: Memory — stack, heap, references
cs-memory.why: Not knowing copy from reference gives you the same bug in every language.
cs-memory.check: You can draw when a value gets copied

cs-os.title: Operating systems — processes, threads, scheduling
cs-os.why: The eye that tells whether slow means CPU or I/O.
cs-os.check: You explain blocking vs non-blocking with an example

cs-ds.title: Data structures
cs-ds.why: Change the structure and the algorithm often disappears entirely.
cs-ds.check: You choose between array, hash and tree and say why

cs-algo.title: Algorithms and complexity
cs-algo.why: The moment where O(n²) has to become O(n log n) really does arrive.
cs-algo.check: You state the complexity of your own code out loud

cs-concurrency.title: Concurrency — races and locks
cs-concurrency.why: Home of the bug that fails only sometimes. This is why it will not reproduce.
cs-concurrency.check: You cause a race condition on purpose

cs-net.title: Networking — IP, TCP, DNS, TLS
cs-net.why: Every web problem eventually lands on one of those four.
cs-net.check: You narrate what happens after you press enter in the address bar

cs-db.title: Databases — indexes and transactions
cs-db.why: One slow query stops the whole service. An index is a data structure, not magic.
cs-db.check: You read a query plan and pick an index

cs-compiler.title: How a language runs — parser and runtime
cs-compiler.why: Build one and "language" stops being mystical.
cs-compiler.check: You write a small calculator interpreter

shell-fs.title: File system and paths
shell-fs.why: Everything branches from that first slash. Confuse absolute and relative and every command is a gamble.
shell-fs.check: With cd, ls and find alone you locate a log on someone else's server

shell-perm.title: Permissions and ownership
shell-perm.why: "Permission denied" is not an error, it is a design. You have to read why it stopped you.
shell-perm.check: You convert between rwx and chmod numbers both ways

shell-editor.title: Terminal editors (vim, nano)
shell-editor.why: Your editor is not on the server. You should at least know how to get out.
shell-editor.check: You edit one line of a config file, save it, and leave

shell-pipe.title: Pipes, grep, sed, awk
shell-pipe.why: Chaining small tools is the whole of Unix. You stop needing to buy a log analyzer.
shell-pipe.check: You pull the top 10 errors from a log in one line

shell-proc.title: Processes, ports, resources
shell-proc.why: To answer "the server feels slow" you must see what holds CPU, memory and ports.
shell-proc.check: You name the guilty process using ps, top and lsof

shell-ssh.title: SSH, keys, remote work
shell-ssh.why: While you are typing passwords, automation stays impossible.
shell-ssh.check: You log in with a key and open a remote screen through port forwarding

shell-script.title: Shell scripts and cron
shell-script.why: Done twice, script it. Done daily, schedule it. By hand you will eventually skip it.
shell-script.check: Your backup runs as a script every day

devops-container.title: Containers (Docker)
devops-container.why: The tool that ends "works on my machine". The environment becomes code.
devops-container.check: Your app becomes an image and runs the same on another machine

devops-env.title: Config and secrets
devops-env.why: The moment a token lands in the code, that repository is polluted for good.
devops-env.check: Values live outside the code, in env vars and a secret store

devops-ci.title: CI — checks on every push
devops-ci.why: A check people have to remember to run eventually stops running.
devops-ci.check: Tests and lint run automatically on every PR

devops-cd.title: CD — deploy and rollback
devops-cd.why: A deploy you cannot undo is a gamble, not a deploy.
devops-cd.check: One command puts the previous version back

devops-iac.title: Infrastructure as code
devops-iac.why: Infrastructure built by clicking is infrastructure nobody can reproduce.
devops-iac.check: You stand up one server from code and tear it down

devops-obs.title: Logs, metrics, traces
devops-obs.why: The worst outage is the one your users know about before you do.
devops-obs.check: An alert reaches you when the error rate spikes

devops-postmortem.title: Incident response and postmortems
devops-postmortem.why: The same outage twice is not an accident, it is a habit.
devops-postmortem.check: You write cause and prevention without blaming a person

sec-owasp.title: The common holes (OWASP Top 10)
sec-owasp.why: Most real incidents are not novel techniques — they are these ten.
sec-owasp.check: You point at where injection or XSS could land in your code

sec-authn.title: Authentication is not authorization
sec-authn.why: Mix up who you are with what you may do and other people's data shows up.
sec-authn.check: You put someone else's id into your API and confirm it is refused

sec-secret.title: Handling secrets
sec-secret.why: A token that entered git history stays there after you delete it.
sec-secret.check: A check catches secrets before the commit

sec-crypto.title: Crypto basics — hashing, symmetric, public key
sec-crypto.why: You need the principles if only to understand why not to roll your own.
sec-crypto.check: You explain why passwords are stored as a salted hash

sec-supply.title: Supply chain — dependencies
sec-supply.why: Code you never wrote runs inside your service.
sec-supply.check: You receive dependency vulnerability alerts and act on them

sec-practice.title: Break something yourself
sec-practice.why: Reading defense alone teaches little. Break in once and code looks different.
sec-practice.check: You solve a wargame level on your own

ai-token.title: Tokens, context window, cost
ai-token.why: Length, price and speed are all decided here. Skip it and the invoice teaches you.
ai-token.check: You compute the token count and cost of one request

ai-prompt.title: A prompt is a spec
ai-prompt.why: Vague instructions produce vague output. Same as handing work to a person.
ai-prompt.check: You tighten the instruction until the same input stops wobbling

ai-limits.title: Hallucination and limits
ai-limits.why: Models are bad at saying they do not know. The system has to cover that.
ai-limits.check: You write down where wrong answers will appear and plan for it

ai-rag.title: Adding retrieval (embeddings, RAG)
ai-rag.why: The usual way to put your own data into a model that never saw it.
ai-rag.check: You ask your document pile a question and get the source passage back

ai-tools.title: Tool use and agents
ai-tools.why: Where the model stops talking and starts doing — and where safety design begins.
ai-tools.check: You attach one tool and decide what happens when it fails

ai-eval.title: Evaluation — measuring the gain
ai-eval.why: The feeling that a prompt got better is usually wrong.
ai-eval.check: You score 20 fixed cases and compare

data-model.title: Modeling — how to split the tables
data-model.why: A schema is the decision you cannot change later. Get it wrong and the code compensates forever.
data-model.check: You normalize, and say where you deliberately break it

data-sql.title: SQL — joins, aggregates, window functions
data-sql.why: The moment you pull it into the app and loop, you are doing the database's job slowly.
data-sql.check: You produce a report with three joins and a group by

data-tx.title: Transactions and isolation levels
data-tx.why: The bug where money leaves twice usually starts here.
data-tx.check: You give an example of a phantom read

data-cache.title: Cache — invalidation is the real work
data-cache.why: Adding a cache is easy. Without a rule for dropping it you serve wrong answers fast.
data-cache.check: You write the cache key and expiry rule before adding it

data-queue.title: Queues and async work
data-queue.why: Do slow work inside the request and the user waits. Push it aside and do it later.
data-queue.check: Failed jobs retry, but not forever

data-format.title: Shapes on the wire — JSON, CSV, schema
data-format.why: Most integration incidents are not algorithms, they are "the shape differs".
data-format.check: You document the schema of the data you hand over

game-loop.title: Game loop and delta time
game-loop.why: A world that ticks per frame. Skip delta and characters teleport on a fast machine.
game-loop.check: Movement speed stays the same when the frame rate wobbles

game-engine.title: One engine (Unity / Godot)
game-engine.why: The engine is a tool, not the goal. Finish with one and you can read the others.
game-engine.check: You build a moving character and a wall that stops it

game-input.title: Input and state machines
game-input.why: How a game feels comes down to when input is taken and when it lands.
game-input.check: You turn overlaps like attacking mid-jump into explicit rules

game-feel.title: Game feel — effects and impact
game-feel.why: The same logic becomes a different game with shake, sound and one frozen frame.
game-feel.check: You toggle the effects off and on and describe the difference

game-balance.title: Numbers and balance
game-balance.why: Numbers in code turn tuning into a deploy. Pull them into a table and the game comes alive.

game-ship.title: Finishing and releasing
game-ship.why: One finished game teaches far more than ten half-built ones.
game-ship.check: Someone else installs it and plays to the end

craft-debug.title: Debugging is narrowing hypotheses
craft-debug.why: A bug fixed by poking comes back. The procedure for narrowing is the skill.
craft-debug.check: You write three hypotheses and start by ruling one out

craft-read.title: Reading other people's code
craft-read.why: Most of the job is reading, not writing. Reading speed is your speed.
craft-read.check: You follow one feature through an unfamiliar repository

craft-refactor.title: Refactoring — changing without breaking
craft-refactor.why: Refactoring without tests is just rewriting.
craft-refactor.check: You separate behavior-preserving changes from behavior-changing ones by commit

craft-doc.title: Documentation and naming
craft-doc.why: You in six months is a stranger. A name and one line save that person.
craft-doc.check: Someone else runs it from the README alone

craft-ask.title: How to ask
craft-ask.why: A good question has already solved half of itself before the answer arrives.
craft-ask.check: You bring repro steps, expected and actual
links: How to ask questions the smart way

craft-ai.title: Working with AI
craft-ai.why: Take it without checking and you get wrong fast. It is about what to delegate and what to verify.
craft-ai.check: You verify AI-written code with a test before committing

craft-focus.title: Focus and consistency
craft-focus.why: This breaks before the technical skills do. Thirty minutes a day beats a weekend sprint.
craft-focus.check: You sit down five times a week at a set time

mobile-choice.title: Native, cross-platform or web
mobile-choice.why: There is no answer to "which is better", only a choice of what to give up.
mobile-choice.check: You choose based on whether you need camera, notifications or offline

mobile-pwa.title: PWA — the web that installs
mobile-pwa.why: It reaches the home screen with no store review. The shortest path for a web developer.
mobile-pwa.check: Your site installs and opens from an icon

mobile-touch.title: Touch and finger size
mobile-touch.why: Buttons designed for a mouse do not fit a thumb. 44px is a spec, not a taste.
mobile-touch.check: You finish the main action one-handed with your thumb

mobile-offline.title: Offline and slow networks
mobile-offline.why: It cuts out on the subway. What you show when it does is the quality of the app.
mobile-offline.check: It still shows something in airplane mode

mobile-perf.title: Battery and performance
mobile-perf.why: Costs invisible on a desktop all surface here.
mobile-perf.check: You measure first paint on a slow device (4x throttle)

mobile-notify.title: Notifications — permission and manners
mobile-notify.why: An app that asks for everything up front gets deleted.
mobile-notify.check: You explain on screen why to enable it, then ask

mobile-store.title: Store release and review
mobile-store.why: Between building and shipping sit signing, review and privacy labels.
mobile-store.check: A test release installs on someone else's device

scale-measure.title: Measure first — load testing
scale-measure.why: Guess at the slow part and you will fix the wrong thing three times.
scale-measure.check: You state requests per second and latency spread (p50, p95)

scale-vertical.title: Growing one machine is also an answer
scale-vertical.why: Distribution costs. If a bigger server solves it, that is usually cheaper.
scale-vertical.check: You give the ceiling of vertical scaling in numbers

scale-lb.title: Load balancers and statelessness
scale-lb.why: If the server holds memory, everything drifts from the second machine on.
scale-lb.check: You move sessions out of the server

scale-cap.title: CAP and eventual consistency
scale-cap.why: Once it is partitioned you must pick between always current and always answering.
scale-cap.check: You say which side your service chose

scale-shard.title: Sharding and replication
scale-shard.why: How you split the data decides which queries you can no longer run.
scale-shard.check: You choose a shard key and explain the price

scale-fail.title: Containing failure — timeouts and circuit breakers
scale-fail.why: One slow place drags everything down with it. Cutting failure early is the defense.
scale-fail.check: Your service answers even when a dependency is dead

gfx-pipeline.title: Render pipeline — vertex to pixel
gfx-pipeline.why: If you cannot tell whether "it is heavy" means vertices or pixels, every optimization is a gamble.
gfx-pipeline.check: You name draw call, vertex and fragment stages in order

gfx-space.title: Coordinate spaces and matrices
gfx-space.why: 99% of objects vanishing or flipping comes from losing track of which space you are in.
gfx-space.check: You explain model, view and projection transforms in order

gfx-shader.title: Shaders — tiny programs on the GPU
gfx-shader.why: Written with a CPU mindset they crawl. This is where "millions at once" enters your hands.
gfx-shader.check: You write a fragment shader that shifts color over time

gfx-light.title: Light and materials (PBR)
gfx-light.why: Why the same model looks different per game. Physically based means there are rules.
gfx-light.check: You change roughness and metalness and predict the result

gfx-color.title: Color spaces and gamma
gfx-color.why: The answer to "why does it look washed out only in Unity". Mix linear and sRGB and color collapses.
gfx-color.check: You explain why a linear workflow is needed

gfx-perf.title: Profiling — what eats the frame
gfx-perf.why: Bottlenecks guessed by eye are usually wrong, especially on the GPU.
gfx-perf.check: You separate CPU-bound from GPU-bound with a tool

embed-mcu.title: MCU and GPIO — wiggling one pin
embed-mcu.why: First time you touch electricity with code. One LED lighting up opens everything after it.
embed-mcu.check: A button press turns an LED on

embed-limit.title: Resource limits — memory and power
embed-limit.why: Kilobytes and a battery decide the design. PC instincts break here.
embed-limit.check: You explain why dynamic allocation is avoided

embed-rt.title: Interrupts and real time
embed-rt.why: "It freezes sometimes" usually means you stayed too long inside an interrupt.
embed-rt.check: You list what must not happen in an interrupt handler

embed-bus.title: Buses — UART, I2C, SPI
embed-bus.why: When a sensor will not answer, the eye that tells wiring from protocol.
embed-bus.check: You read the signal on a logic analyzer

embed-net.title: IoT — MQTT and wireless
embed-net.why: Flaky links, batteries, untrusted networks. Web assumptions do not hold here.
embed-net.check: Data survives a disconnect and reconnect

embed-ota.title: Firmware updates (OTA)
embed-ota.why: A machine you cannot fix ends up in a box. This is also where bricking on a failed update is prevented.
embed-ota.check: It recovers even when an update is cut off midway
